formulations.note: No UK povidone-iodine ointment was found (emc and MHRA products searched). This entry uses the UK 5% w/w cream SPC: same ingredient and skin route, but a different strength and base. The amounts in the dosing items (pea-sized amounts, maximum by age) are for the 5% cream and cannot be applied directly to the 10% ointment; use the clinic product label for the amount. The UK 10% product is an alcoholic tincture for skin disinfection before surgery and was not used.

items.t: Cream (UK): clean and dry the wound; apply a small pea-sized amount once or twice daily for up to 7 consecutive days. The daily application must not cover more than 1% of total body surface area. Adult maximum: 8 to 9 pea-sized amounts twice a day.

src.q: Apply a small pea sized amount to the affected area (once or twice daily) up to a maximum of 7 consecutive days.
The maximum daily application should not exceed over 1% of the total body surface area.
Adults 8-9 small pea sized amount twice a day

items.t: Spray powder: adults and children over 2 years: clean the wound, spray evenly for 3 seconds from 15 cm, once or twice a day for up to 7 consecutive days.

src.q: Spray evenly onto the wound area for three (3) seconds from a distance of 15 cm (6 inches).
Apply the spray once or twice a day for up to 7 consecutive days.

items.t: Fire risk: fabric that has been in contact with the cream burns more easily (no smoking or naked flames); the spray propellant is flammable, and electrocautery should wait until the spray mist has gone.

src.q: Do not smoke or go near naked flames - risk of severe burns.
that has been in contact with this product burns more easily and is a serious fire hazard
The propellant gases are flammable, keep away from heat, hot surfaces, sparks, open flames.
Electrocautery should only be used after spray mist has completely vanished.

items.t: Silver-containing products (such as silver sulfadiazine), hydrogen peroxide and taurolidine: mutual reduction of effect; the SPCs say povidone-iodine should not be used together with silver salts.

src.q: Products containing mercury, silver, hydrogen peroxide, and taurolidine may interact with povidone-iodine and cause mutual reduction of effects.
Povidone-iodine should not be used together with alkali, hydrogen peroxide, taurolidine, tannic acid, and silver and mercury salts.
Povidone-Iodine should not be used together with alkali, hydrogen peroxide, taurolidine, tannic acid, and silver and mercury salts.

items.t: Lithium: avoid prolonged use, especially on large areas, as more iodine may be absorbed (spray SPC). Lithium is not in this checker's medicine list.

src.q: Prolonged use, especially on extensive surfaces, should be avoided in patients undergoing lithium therapy as larger amounts of iodine may be absorbed.

items.t: Thyroid tests and radioiodine: iodine absorption can lower thyroid radioiodine uptake and interfere with thyroid scans, protein-bound iodine tests and radioiodine therapy. Allow 4 weeks after treatment before a new scan.

src.q: Absorption of iodine from povidone iodine cream may lower the radioiodine uptake of the thyroid.
After the end of the treatment, 4 weeks should be allowed before a new scintigram is carried out

items.t: Enzymatic wound preparations: both are weakened. Octenidine before or after: transient dark skin discoloration. Lab tests (toluidine, guaiac for blood or glucose in stool or urine) may give false positives.

src.q: The concomitant use of wound-treatment preparations containing enzymatic components leads to a weakening effect of both substances.
Povidone-iodine products when used before or after application of octenidine may lead to transient dark discolorations at the application sites.
various diagnostic agents can show false-positive lab results

items.t: No renal dose advice in the UK SPCs. Acute renal failure may occur after uptake of large amounts (e.g. treating burns).

items.t: Insufficient data. Absorbed iodine crosses the placenta. Use only if the clinical condition requires it and only if clearly necessary, after a benefit/risk assessment.

src.q: There is insufficient data on the use of povidone iodine during pregnancy.
Absorbed iodine has been shown to cross the placental barrier
should only be used if the clinical condition of the woman requires treatment with povidone iodine

items.t: Should not be used during breastfeeding: iodine concentrates in breast milk and may cause transient hypothyroidism with raised TSH in the newborn; the baby's thyroid function may need checking.

src.q: Betadine Cream should not be used during breastfeeding.
Absorbed iodine is excreted in breast milk to such an extent that effects on breastfed newborns are likely.
may induce transient hypothyroidism with elevation of TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone) in the newborn
a check of the child's thyroid function may be necessary

items.t: The same SPCs (section 4.4) also allow use when breastfeeding only if clearly necessary after a benefit/risk assessment, on a doctor's advice.

src.q: if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, unless advised to do so by your doctor
